json.root: Sets JSON output for bare list and commands that merge root flags. Does not work for root-prefixed skills/init/index in the current implementation.
json.list: One derived session metadata object per output line. Not original transcript JSONL. Timestamp strings are display-formatted.
json.show: Complete original source JSONL objects for selected events, deduplicated by physical sequence. Selection still applies. Raw siblings within a selected record remain present.
json.prompts: Complete original source JSONL objects for selected prompt events, deduplicated by physical sequence. A raw record can contain sibling non-prompt blocks.
json.errors: Complete original source JSONL objects for selected errors, deduplicated by physical sequence after error selection.
json.tools: One derived type=tools aggregate containing calls, errors and skill_inputs. No source session identity. -n does not trim its keys.
json.stats: One derived type=stats object per selected session. Counts include human-formatted strings such as tokens and size.
json.path: One type=path object per distinct selected path.
json.grep: Without -c/-l, one original source JSONL object per matching normalized event, so one physical record can repeat. -c emits grep_count aggregates. -l overrides JSON and prints plain IDs.
json.cmds: One original source JSONL object per tool call, potentially repeated when a source record contains multiple calls. Paired result state is not added to the raw record.
json.find: One structured envelope with results (or paths), total, complete, coverage and errors. Evidence is bounded excerpts, not whole raw records.
json.skills: One structured envelope with grouped skills, totals, completeness, errors, coverage and index metadata. Overrides text --paths rendering.
json.secrets: One masked type=secret object per distinct fingerprint. Raw values never printed.
json.secrets audit: One masked type=secret object per distinct fingerprint. Raw values never printed.
json.secrets clean: One masked type=clean object per changed physical file, with counts and applied flag. Completion/skip/failure totals are printed on stderr, not as JSON records.

root: Keep -n as session count for bare list and pass it only to compatible commands.
list: Session rows in text and metadata objects in JSON
Keep the session unit and include explicit omitted counts in JSON mode.
show: Normalized events in text, distinct physical source records in JSON
Make the limit unit explicit per format and keep complete raw records. Never drop sibling events from a selected raw record.
prompts: Prompt events in text, distinct physical source records in JSON
Keep all human prompts by default. Explicit -n caps selected prompts only. Proposed --all lifts presentation limits without changing provenance selection.
errors: Error events in text, distinct physical error source records in JSON, globally across sessions
Keep a global error-result cap and complete raw JSON records. Include source identity in text.
tools: Tool-name rows in text. JSON always emits one complete aggregate
Count tool entries in either format and include total/omitted metadata if JSON is capped.
stats: Field/value rows in text, complete session objects in JSON
Count complete session summaries consistently in text and JSON.
path: Distinct file paths in either format
Keep a global cap after path deduplication and continue reporting omissions on stderr.
grep: Match rows, context windows, matching IDs or count-table sessions according to output mode. 0 also disables match budget
all rows, budget still applies unless -n 0
Define the unit for each mode. Make -n 0 remove only the count cap and use --all for wholly uncapped output.
cmds: Tool call rows globally across sessions. JSON may duplicate a physical record
Keep a global call cap for text/events JSON. Deduplicate whole source records before applying raw JSON limits.
find: Matching sessions, or source paths in --paths mode
Retain 5 ranked sessions and unlimited path default. 0 explicitly means all results. Show the defaults in both parser help paths.
skills: Content groups, or physical files with --copies, before alias expansion
Keep 20 normal results. In path mode cap distinct emitted paths after expansion, and honor inherited root limits.
secrets: Distinct secret fingerprints after full-scope tally
Keep output-only cap with full-scope counts and explicit omitted count.
secrets audit: Distinct secret fingerprints after full-scope tally
Keep output-only cap with full-scope counts and explicit omitted count.
secrets clean: Changed-file report rows. All selected files are still scanned and, with --apply, rewritten
Retain display-only limit. Spell out that this is not a maximum number of files to rewrite.

show arg: Newest session by default. Accepts @N, inclusive @A:@B range, unique ID prefix or unique name. Implementation silently reads only the first resolved reference.
Honor all selected sessions and identify each in output.
prompts arg: Newest session by default. Accepts @N, inclusive range, unique ID prefix or unique name. Implementation silently reads only the first resolved reference.
Honor all selected sessions with source identity and complete human prompt text.
tools arg: Newest session by default. Accepts a range but silently reads only the first reference.
Honor each selected session and identify its tool summary.
errors arg: Newest session by default. Resolves all references in a range, preserving scope order.
Retain range support and put source session/sequence on every result.
stats arg: Newest session by default. A range yields separate session statistics.
Retain selection and use whole-session limit units.
path arg: Newest session by default. A range yields all selected provider paths, deduplicated.
Retain range support and exact path output.
grep arg: Optional second positional selects sessions. Omitted means all in scope. -e makes the first positional the selector instead.
Retain explicit scope and the targeted unquoted-pattern error. Document the -e shift.
grep pattern: One smart-case regex positional, optional only when --regexp/-e supplies it. Invalid regex exits 2. -F enables literal substring matching.
Retain one-pattern grammar and helpful errors. Do not guess whether a second word is a session.
cmds arg: Newest session by default, except nonempty --grep with no selector scans every session. A range selects all its references.
Keep newest as the stable default and add explicit --all-sessions for cross-session command search.
find query: One optional shell argument containing up to 12 distinct word or quoted-phrase clues. Required unless --index. Inner parsing uses shell-style quoting and drops punctuation-only clues.
Accept QUERY... arguments while preserving the existing single-string and quoted-phrase grammar. Keep the 12-clue bound with a clear diagnostic.
skills query: One optional query string, default empty. Path/name substring clues are case-insensitive. Colons are treated as clue separators. Exact directory names rank first.
Accept multiple clue arguments and preserve current name/path matching. Explain --exact applies to names.
init file: Optional target file used only with --write/--check. Otherwise nearest AGENTS.md or --global fallback. Mutually exclusive with --global.
Keep explicit file targeting and current fallback. State the resolved destination in output.
secrets audit arg: Omitted audits every session in scope. Selectors support @N, ranges, unique prefixes and names. Shorthand secrets SESSION forwards here.
Retain whole-scope default and shorthand. Expose audit in help so reserved action names are clear.
secrets clean arg: Omitted cleans/previews all references in scope, then expands physical copies and Claude children. A range selects references before expansion.
Define physical scope identically across audit/preview/apply and preserve that selection in follow-up commands.
serve action: Optional status or stop, default status. Typer declares an unconstrained string and delegates validation. --foreground bypasses the action in the fast parser.
Declare one shared choice type and validate internal foreground launch separately.
